noticias.titulo: Are Amazon drones about to take over the skies?
noticias.descripcion: STORY: :: take over the skies? Are Amazon drones about to take over the skies? :: Amazon's big plans for drone deliveries :: 500 :: tens of millions Amazon says it plans to expand drone deliveries to nearly 500 US cities and towns by the end of this year, reaching tens of millions of customers. Jeff Bezos first unveiled Amazon’s ‘octocopters’ back in 2013, predicting they’d be delivering packages within four or five years. Well, that took a little longer than planned. The program has faced regulatory delays, staff cuts, technical problems - and some pretty spectacular mishaps. :: a viral hit Two drones have collided. And one dropped a package straight into a customer’s swimming pool - a viral hit. :: hurdles to clear There’s still plenty of hurdles to clear. Amazon needs approval from communities one by one - sitting through local council meetings and answering questions from residents. In Nampa, Idaho, Amazon was grilled for about an hour over noise, safety and bird protection. :: approve the rollout The company said its drones would only be audible as they arrive and leave - quieter than a lawnmower. The board ultimately voted to approve the rollout. So, Amazon wants to turn drone delivery from a futuristic idea into a key part of its speedy delivery network. One day, your package could arrive just minutes after you order it. But first, you might have to get used to the noise.

Utilities/Energy.descripcion: NextEra Energy (NYSE:NEE) faces new regulatory attention as Maryland's Office of People's Counsel moves to join federal review of its proposed merger with Dominion Energy. The state watchdog is seeking participation in Federal Energy Regulatory Commission proceedings to assess potential effects on competition in the PJM regional power market. Consumer advocates in Maryland aim to examine how the transaction could influence electricity prices, service reliability, and market concentration...
